source_conflicts.nccp: NCCP v2 says capsules must not be opened or dissolved.
source_conflicts.smpc: Current SmPC permits pharmacist-directed capsule suspension and enteral administration.
source_conflicts.resolution: Standard suite uses whole capsules. Swallowing difficulty or a different formulation requires pharmacy instructions; no unsupervised substitution.

source_conflicts.nccp: Eligibility says age >18 and lists patients with CNS involvement under ROS1.
source_conflicts.smpc: Adult ROS1 indication does not require CNS involvement; the adult trial enrolled age >=18.
source_conflicts.resolution: At age exactly18 or ROS1 without CNS involvement, verify MAP/source interpretation; do not invent an absolute prohibition.

metadata.schedule_summary: The usual adult starting dose is 600 mg by mouth once daily, every day without a planned rest week. Use your prescribed dose. Treatment continues while helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of cycles.

indications.description: ROS1-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer not previously treated with a ROS1 inhibitor.

Adult NTRK gene-fusion-positive locally advanced or metastatic solid tumour, or tumour where resection is likely to cause severe morbidity, after no prior NTRK inhibitor and with no satisfactory treatment option.

treatment.schedule_summary: Entrectinib 600 mg orally once daily continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity; prescribed dose may be reduced.
treatment.duration_text: Continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity
administration_instructions: With or without food. Swallow whole capsules; no crushing or chewing. Pharmacist-directed suspension is a separate current-SmPC method.
Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit products and Seville oranges.
Missed dose: make up unless next dose is due within 12 hours. Immediate vomiting after whole capsules may permit a repeat dose; for suspension seek professional advice.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

rash_grade.label: Rash/skin toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Papules/pustules covering under 10% body-surface area, with or without pruritus or tenderness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Papules/pustules covering 10-30% body-surface area with or without symptoms and psychosocial/instrumental-ADL impact, or over 30% with mild symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Papules/pustules covering over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, limiting self-care ADL, or local superinfection requiring oral antibiotics.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, or extensive superinfection requiring IV antibiotics.

eligibility: Confirm exact adult ROS1 00702a or adult NTRK 00702b indication, validated fusion, previous targeted therapy and current managed access criteria.
NCCP prints age >18, ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ function. At age exactly18 verify adult/MAP interpretation.
NTRK requires no known acquired resistance mutation and no satisfactory treatment option.
exclusions: Hypersensitivity, pregnancy/lactation, prolonged QTc, pre-existing ILD/fibrosis or history of TKI pneumonitis.
Prior ROS1 inhibitor for 00702a; prior NTRK inhibitor for 00702b.
monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal/liver profile, uric acid, ECG/electrolytes, cognition; LVEF with CHF symptoms/risk. Brain imaging per Consultant.
Regular FBC, renal/liver profile, uric acid; ECG/electrolytes after one month then periodically as indicated.
Assess cognition, CHF symptoms, visual changes, fractures, adherence and interactions; disease assessment follows Consultant plan.
dose_modifications: NCCP CTCAE v4.0 event-specific holds, recovery windows and permanent-stop criteria; do not infer recovery or multiply reductions.
Toxicity ladder 600→400→200 mg daily; inability to tolerate200 mg means permanent stop. Temporary CYP3A inhibitor doses 100/200 mg are separate.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00702 v2 minimal-to-low; individual oral support with QT/interactions review. NCIS V8 parenteral regimens are not copied.
